what_happened.text: On Aug. 24, 2026, NASA Earth Observatory published an Image of the Day on ancient Lake Bonneville. A Landsat 8 OLI scene shows pale playa and salt-flat deposits plus bathtub-like rings and wave-cut terraces of former shorelines. The piece recounts the lake’s Ice Age rise and fall and ties the leftover flats to mining, a 2026 Venus-instrument field test, speed runs, and the 1846 Donner-Reed crossing.

why_it_matters_now.text: The hook is current NASA communication: a 2026 satellite image of Ice Age shorelines, plus June 2026 DAVINCI camera rehearsals at Crater Island and an August 2026 hydrogen land-speed mark on the same leftover flats. The discussion should keep those dated NASA claims distinct from broader meaning about climate, Venus, or exploration.

verified_facts.text: NASA says Ice Age Lake Bonneville was nearly as large as Lake Michigan and covered much of western Utah plus parts of Nevada and Idaho.

The article dates lake formation to about 55,000 years ago after eruptions in today’s southeastern Idaho diverted the Bear River; a dam at Red Rock Pass confined the water until a breach about 18,000 years ago sent a flood into the Columbia system and dropped lake level more than 350 feet (105 meters) in about six weeks.

Later warming and drying left remnants NASA names as Great Salt Lake, Utah Lake, and Sevier Lake; Landsat 8 imagery shows former shoreline rings, wave-cut terraces, pale fine-grained lakebed, and bright evaporite salt flats.

In June 2026, DAVINCI teams field-tested descent cameras at Crater Island from a helicopter and, using only those images, made 3-D maps NASA says matched existing geologic maps as practice for Venus’s Alpha Regio.

NASA reports Mickey Thompson hit 406.60 mph on the Bonneville Salt Flats in 1960, Andy Green reached 406.320 mph in a hydrogen-fueled car in August 2026, and the Donner-Reed Party’s wagons broke through thin salt crust near Crater Island in August 1846.

tension_or_argument.text: The article proves a present-day satellite view of shoreline terraces, pale lakebed, and salt-flat mining ponds; the Ice Age chronology, flood, remnant lakes, Venus analogy, and adventure tales are interpretation layered on that landscape. Keep mapped leftovers separate from those stories.

surprising_details.text: NASA frames the Red Rock Pass failure as one of North America’s largest floods, dropping the lake more than 350 feet in six weeks—not a slow fade.
Crater Island is nicknamed “Venus on Earth” for DAVINCI camera tests of iron-rich and silica-rich rocks.
Two headline Bonneville speed marks cited are almost the same number: 406.60 mph in 1960 and 406.320 mph in 2026, the later run burning hydrogen with no carbon dioxide.
Potash evaporation ponds sit on the same playa that trapped Donner-Reed wagons in mud under a thin salt crust.

flexible_outline.text: Open on the Aug. 24, 2026 Landsat 8 image: pale playa versus darker mountains, bathtub rings and wave-cut terraces as the visible leftover shorelines.

Walk the article’s lake timeline only as NASA tells it: ~55,000-year start, Red Rock Pass dam, ~18,000-year breach and 350-foot six-week drop, then climate shrinkage to Great Salt Lake, Utah Lake, and Sevier Lake.
Flag what the image supports (shorelines, evaporites, ponds, old ranges) versus retold history and mission color. Do not treat the feature as a new lake-level proof paper.
June 2026 DAVINCI helicopter descent at Crater Island: cameras, 3-D maps matching geologic maps, Alpha Regio analog.
Salt-flat minerals and rectangular potash ponds as the industrial leftover of evaporation.
Optional color only: Thompson 1960, Green’s August 2026 hydrogen run, Donner-Reed wagons through the crust. Cut if the image and flood timeline fill the clock.
